title: Independence and intrinsic meaning of the resolution construction
as_he_states: “one should check that ... Q together with (10) does not depend on the choice of the resolution” (57:5–6); the coefficient-field dependence is explicitly retained.
plausible_today: Compare local Picard sheaves from two proper regular models by a common dominating model, while fixing the coefficient field and the topology on test algebras.
state_of_art: Boutot gives intrinsic local-Picard theory in specified settings; Kollár states the S₂, pure-dimensional geometric hypotheses. Lipman supplies the local-Artin comparison.
why_open: No longer an open existence program in those settings. The letter’s unrestricted completed tensor-product formulation still needs its exact hypotheses, and independence of a model is not independence of a coefficient field.
worth: High editorial value; first write the comparison diagram including the twisted exceptional lattice and Brauer boundary.

title: Positive exceptional model and stabilization
as_he_states: “replacing if necessary X by a suitable model dominating it ... J/J² [is] an ample sheaf” (57:7).
plausible_today: Ask for a projective birational model with an invertible exceptional ideal of ample conormal, and separately prove stabilization of its formal Picard system.
state_of_art: The conditional stabilization follows from Serre vanishing and square-zero units; surface negativity and local Picard theory provide established cases.
why_open: The computation proves the consequence, not the existence of the required model in every version of the letter’s hypotheses.
worth: Medium; determine the intended birational/projectivity assumptions before any new theorem is sought.

title: Exceptional lattice injectivity in higher dimension
as_he_states: “It would be nice to have a proof in general ... negative definiteness of an intersection matrix Xᶦ.Cʲ?” (57:8).
plausible_today: Under precise projective birational hypotheses, test whether exceptional Cartier divisors inject into the special-fibre Néron–Severi group.
state_of_art: Normal surface negative definiteness proves the stated surface case. General local-Picard quotient descriptions require their specified geometric assumptions.
why_open: A general higher-dimensional negativity theorem has not been matched to the exact draft formulation by this search.
worth: Medium; identify a modern negativity lemma whose hypotheses match the chosen model, then compare its kernel with the lattice in the letter.

title: Functor on arbitrary test algebras
as_he_states: The formula (18) is offered “more or less”; the actual Picard interpretation on57:9–11 is proved only for noetherian geometrically regular test algebras.
plausible_today: Specify the topology and derived or ordinary completed base change before extending the representing-property claim to all algebras.
state_of_art: The intrinsic functor exists in Boutot’s setting. The letter itself distinguishes sheafification from actual Picard groups and records a Brauer obstruction.
why_open: The wider test-category assertion is not verified merely by checking geometric points or tangent spaces.
worth: High for consolidation; compare the exact functor in Boutot with formula(18), one test-category restriction at a time.

title: Mixed-characteristic Artin-base Picard group
as_he_states: “Let A be a local Artin ring with perfect residue field k ... Give a natural construction” (57:11), followed by the Greenberg ring-functor candidate on57:12.
plausible_today: Construct the locally algebraic group of a proper scheme over a local Artin ring through the relevant Greenberg/Witt-vector functor and compare rational points.
state_of_art: Lipman1976 identifies Grothendieck’s September1969 question and answers it; Theorem1.2 and§5 give the construction and Theorem7.5 the descent obstruction.
why_open: Solved in the cited hypotheses. The source’s original literal injection must be read together with its obstruction statement.
worth: High historical match; first align the letter’s formula(22) with Lipman’s exact sequence.

title: Cube calculation and the correspondence splitting
as_he_states: The pages solve the recurrence for αₙ and repeatedly recompute the n-factor formula; the exact product sequence is marked “split” when all factors have sections (57:15–19).
plausible_today: Use unordered pairs and normalized restrictions to write the cube identity and the Picard-product decomposition with the precise properness and H⁰ assumptions.
state_of_art: Classical cube theory; coefficients were independently recomputed. The correspondence functor’s infinitesimal rigidity is separate from its general separatedness.
why_open: No open arithmetic recurrence remains. Pair-index ink and the scope of representability are editorial checks.
worth: High for error prevention; verify n=3 before interpreting the general exponent formula.

title: Extend an abelian group law through a proper smooth family
as_he_states: 57:33 states the one-abelian-fibre theorem;57:41 reduces closedness to aDVR and says the argument is known but “à développer”.
plausible_today: Fix a section of a smooth proper family and establish that the abelian-scheme locus is open and closed; distinguish the projective theorem from the full proper formulation.
state_of_art: GIT6.14 and Genestier–Ngô2.4.1 give the projective statement. Their infinitesimal andDVR lemmas match the draft’s intermediate steps.
why_open: The opened projective theorem alone does not certify the wider proper statement. The source’s uniqueness proof is stronger than its written existence argument.
worth: High historical reconstruction; locate the proper-family extension theorem and compare the section and connected-base hypotheses.

title: Which groups have dense prime-to-characteristic torsion?
as_he_states: The proposed no-additive-factor criterion is rejected on57:44: “Or ça ...” is followed by the vector-extension counterconsideration;57:51 introduces “très rigide”.
plausible_today: Classify the smooth commutative groups satisfying the exact finite-torsion and schematic-density conditions, keeping connectedness and the prime quantifiers explicit.
state_of_art: Brion’s anti-affine classification explains the characteristic-zero vector extensions; SGA3XI§6 supplies the finite-level density framework.
why_open: The withdrawn necessity is not open. The draft adjective combines several conditions and must be defined before it can be compared with a modern classification.
worth: Medium; translate the definition into separate density, finiteness and smooth-subgroup requirements.

title: Spread rigid subgroup schemes over primary extensions
as_he_states: 57:49 admits the spreading-out rigidity step,57:51 strengthens the definition, and57:53–58 distinguishes descent of support from descent of the subgroup.
plausible_today: Determine when a closed subgroup after a primary extension descends, and when only its smooth reduced support is constant.
state_of_art: SGA3 has precise torsion-density, transporter, quotient and field-extension results; the general draft chain still depends on an admitted lemma.
why_open: The gap is a precise hypothesis comparison. A finite radicial residual quotient can survive even when support is fixed.
worth: Medium; state the spread-out lemma without the undefined adjective and compare it with SGA3XI6.2.

title: Can rigidity force the kernel to be open?
as_he_states: The proposition on57:51 asserting a universally open kernel is crossed out;57:52 exhibits the limiting elliptic graph example.
plausible_today: Identify exactly which flatness or torsion hypotheses prevent specialization of a kernel from acquiring extra components.
state_of_art: The proposed universal statement is already refuted by the author. SGA3 separates openness, flatness and topological surjectivity.
why_open: Not an unsolved conjecture. The remaining task is to preserve the correction and its relation to the earlier unramified-ambient lemma.
worth: High editorial value, low research priority; compare the two ambient group schemes in the purported contradiction.

title: Relative Albanese when the Picard identity component is not proper
as_he_states: 57:60–63 constructs homogeneous and inhomogeneous Albanese objects and asks how far the relative existence argument extends.
plausible_today: Seek a base-change-compatible family of maximal abelian subvarieties ofPic^τ and dualize it to an Albanese torsor, rather than taking a Chevalley quotient.
state_of_art: Laurent–Schröer2024 Th10.2 supplies this criterion; Th7.2 and Cor10.5 handle field-extension and proper-field cases.
why_open: Solved subject to the existence of the indicated family. The criterion itself explains why arbitrary degeneration does not automatically give a relative Albanese scheme.
worth: High; first compare the universal mapping property and maximal-subgroup condition with the draft’s minimal-subgroup construction.

title: Picard smoothness over nonreduced characteristic-zero bases
as_he_states: 57:64 asks whether the characteristic-zero smoothness and cohomological-flatness argument persists over a nonreduced base.
plausible_today: Distinguish Pic⁰ from the full Picard space, and specify whether the family is smooth proper or merely has smooth group fibres.
state_of_art: Deligne1968 Th5.5 and Kleiman5.21 yield smoothPic⁰ in the smooth characteristic-zero setting; Kleiman5.22 gives jumping full-Picard components.
why_open: The identity-component question is settled. A statement about the whole Picard scheme is false without further hypotheses.
worth: High; compare the exact object denotedPic in the sheet with the identity component in the published theorem.

title: Numerical equivalence, boundedness and finite curve tests
as_he_states: 57:71–72 asks which finiteness assertions follow from the equivalence criteria and records Kleiman’s route through numerical classes.
plausible_today: Compare numerical triviality withτ-triviality, establish uniform bounds on geometric NS groups, and test bounded subsets ofPic by degrees on finitely many curves.
state_of_art: FGA236 addendum and SGA6XIII3.6,4.7,5.1–5.4 contain the precise theorems. XIII5.3 directly corrects the factor-two formula on57:70.
why_open: The principal numerical theorems are settled. The isolated external criterion(ii) on57:72 remains underidentified because its antecedent is not supplied.
worth: High historical match; align each numbered statement with its published counterpart rather than treating finiteness as a single assertion.

title: Proper-surjective Picard pullback
as_he_states: The July18,1962 Murre letter asserts finite-type pullback, affineness over fields and generic relative quasi-affineness (57:73–79).
plausible_today: State pullback in the contravariant direction and distinguish finite type, quasi-affine and affine relative representability.
state_of_art: SGA6XII Th1.1 and Cor1.5 give the exact generic and field statements; the full original pages were inspected.
why_open: Settled in those forms. General-base affineness is the distinct MP-SA14-677.
worth: High; use the actual theorem hypotheses in every occurrence of the Murre-letter statement.

title: Universal flattening for proper nonprojective schemes
as_he_states: “Problem A” asks for representability of the base-change functor that makes a coherent sheaf flat (57:74–79).
plausible_today: Represent universal flattening as a monomorphism locally of finite type, keeping properness or an appropriate purity substitute.
state_of_art: Murre1965§3(A) Th2/Cor1 supplies the proper case; Stacks05PS gives the finite-presentation version.
why_open: Solved. A flattening blowup or a convenient stratification is not by itself the universal object asked for.
worth: High; compare the functors on arbitrary test schemes before comparing constructions.

title: Local Picard group of an affine cone
as_he_states: 57:185–192 asks how the cone calculation changes on completing the local ring, after quotienting by the hyperplane class.
plausible_today: Separate the punctured whole cone, the punctured local spectrum and its completion, and compute the positive-twist infinitesimal layers.
state_of_art: Kollár’s cone example and the formal-neighbourhood calculation provide explicit formulas. For a plane curve, the characteristic-zero correction has dimension binomial(d−1,3).
why_open: The curve calculation is settled; the source’s degree≥6 example is sufficient, not minimal. Higher-dimensional obstruction groups need a separate analysis.
worth: High for interpretation; test a smooth plane quartic first, where the correction is already one-dimensional.

title: Punctured henselization versus completion
as_he_states: 57:194: “Il est possible que la dernière flèche ...” proposes Picard invariance under completion of the henselian pair.
plausible_today: Compare isomorphism classes of line bundles on the complement of the defining ideal in a noetherian henselian pair and its completion.
state_of_art: Elkik1973III.1 Th3 and the corollariespp573–574 give the Picard comparison.
why_open: Solved under the cited henselian/noetherian hypotheses. This does not assert equality of unit groups or full faithfulness of the line-bundle groupoid.
worth: High exact match; quote the corollary with its puncture and completion ideal.

title: The σ² torsion-rank criterion for families of abelian components
as_he_states: 57:196,198 proposes a criterion with n divisible byσ² for fibrewise abelian varieties to assemble into a subgroup scheme.
plausible_today: Fix the finite component-quotient length and the flatness/reduced-base assumptions before translating the tentative rank test.
state_of_art: SGA3 component theory and Laurent–Schröer’s maximal-abelian-family criterion are relevant; no identicalσ² test was located.
why_open: The diagram is partly underdetermined, and the numerical test is not proved by the structural references alone.
worth: Medium; recover the exact maps and meanings ofσ from the original scans before attempting a modern theorem.

title: Finiteness of the torsion-component locus
as_he_states: 57:203–212 studiesΓ^τ, bounded torsion exponents and the prime-to-characteristic locus, with a marginal request to provePic^τ quasi-compact.
plausible_today: Separate general group-scheme component statements from the special boundedness theorem for the Picard functor.

why_open: The Picard theorem is settled. Literal component criteria such as “one aⁿ is closed” are insufficient and remain reading alarms.
worth: Medium; test the proposed general criterion on a discrete étale group before invoking Picard-specific boundedness.

title: Finite type from openness and proper fibres
as_he_states: 57:208–209 gives a finite-type criterion and then a constructible-subset version, crossing out “universally” in the first statement.
plausible_today: Prove relative quasi-compactness by spreading a proper generic piece and using openness or generization lifting to eliminate the remainder.
state_of_art: The scheme version has an independent noetherian-induction proof and belongs to EGA’s properness criteria; the exact subset formulation was not identified verbatim.
why_open: The remaining issue is the structure carried by the constructible subset, not the elementary induction once that structure is supplied.
worth: Medium; formulate the subset version as a locally closed subspace before comparing EGA references.

title: What does the degenerating conic show?
as_he_states: The nonrepresentability argument on57:217–218 is withdrawn, and57:219 says the many-origin scheme represents the functor.
plausible_today: Compute special bidegrees, identify classes of equal generic degree and glue one origin for each special multidegree.
state_of_art: The explicit computation gives a nonseparated representable Picard scheme. Vertical component self-intersections are−1.
why_open: No surviving nonrepresentability conjecture remains in this example.
worth: High editorial priority; preserve the cancellation and the final many-origin construction together.

title: Closed-cover Čech computation for three lines
as_he_states: 57:224 proposes H¹(X,O_X)≅H¹(X₁⊔X₂⊔X₃/X,G_a) and adds a strict-descent justification.

why_open: The proposed method is false in this literal form; a correct resolution must include the nonexactness of the closed-cover complex.
worth: High; inspect the common-intersection stalk first and retain the counterexample as a warning against closed-cover Čech arguments.

title: Kummer transgression and the generalized Jacobian torsor
as_he_states: 57:142–145 asks whether the low-degree transgression class equals the Kummer boundary of the generalized degree-one Picard torsor.

why_open: The full relative compact-support statement and its sign were not identified verbatim. Field and semiabelian results do not automatically settle every base in the draft.
worth: High; fix the cohomological triangle and boundary convention, then compare the two cocycles.

title: When is the Picard group of a singular curve abelian?
as_he_states: 57:147–151 revises the graph and singularity contributions to the Picard dimension;57:151 states the converse under the indicated singularity restrictions.

why_open: The normalization calculation is settled. The local symbolμ must not be identified simultaneously with branch number andδ-invariant.
worth: High; test an ordinary node and a cusp before reading the general formula.

title: Dimension of the moduli strata in the curve sketches
as_he_states: 57:153,155 adds the component contributions3gᵢ−3+νᵢ and then introduces unfinished corrections for unstable rational components.

worth: Medium; label every vertex, branch and automorphism dimension in one of the drawn examples.

title: Projective frames versus unmarked embedded varieties
as_he_states: 57:158–162 compares special line bundles, Brauer–Severi bundles and a projective-linear quotient; a marginal condition invokes automorphisms ofX.

worth: High; write the two functors and their automorphism groups before taking a quotient.

title: Check the tangent and obstruction diagram for Div→Pic
as_he_states: 57:164 labels the tangent spaces and says various cohomology vanishings imply smoothness.
plausible_today: Derive the diagram from0→O_X→L→N_D→0 and distinguish relativeDiv/Pic from absoluteDiv/S obstructions.

worth: High as a reading check; reconstruct the long exact sequence before comparing subscripts.

title: Regularity in codimension one and rational-map extension
as_he_states: 57:166–171 introduces pseudo-morphisms and asks for polar-locus descriptions while the target’s affine qualifier is altered.
plausible_today: Separate uniqueness from schematic density, extension at codimension-one points to proper targets, and global regularity of functions on normal schemes.

why_open: The overly broad statements are refuted by explicit examples; the qualified standard results are settled.
worth: High; test the punctured nonnormal surface ring and the rational mapP²⇢P¹ before merging the assertions.

title: Local connectedness under successive cuts
as_he_states: 58:3–17 develops and repeatedly revises the connectedness-dimension induction, including a finite set of points to avoid and a converse.
plausible_today: State the complete-local connectedness theorem with initial connectedness and component-dimension assumptions, then distinguish sufficient and necessary conditions.
state_of_art: SGA2XIII Th2.1 and its following converse discussion are the direct published match. The initial unqualified lemma is false without connectedness.
why_open: The main theorem is published; the draft’s reversed inequality and incomplete induction are reading/proof-status issues.
worth: High historical match; compare the hypotheses line by line withXIII2.1 instead of only citing a generic connectedness theorem.

title: Finite generation of the local fundamental group
as_he_states: 58:19 reduces to normal dimension2 and conjectures finite generation for complete local rings with algebraically closed residue field.
plausible_today: Ask topological finite generation of the full étale fundamental group of the connected punctured spectrum, with the noetherian and dimension conditions explicit.

why_open: The cited partial theorem does not settle the full profinite group. Results for tame quotients or special singularities also do not imply the full assertion.
worth: High research relevance, but first check the exact full-group status after2023 and separate all quotient variants.

title: Determinant descent without a chosen point
as_he_states: 59:2–6 asks to detail descent of the determinant’s NS class and to verify the sign in the resulting three-torsor trivialization.
plausible_today: Fix a determinant convention and normalized Poincaré bundle, then compare the basepoint change by exponent−χ and the induced contracted-torsor cocycle.
state_of_art: Knudsen–Mumford supplies determinant functors and base change; the draft’s NS independence follows. The exact canonical three-torsor comparison was not located verbatim.
why_open: Existence of equal cohomology classes is weaker than an equality of canonical rigidified sections; that last comparison remains explicitly unverified here.
worth: High; write one Čech cocycle for changing the basepoint and check its signs against the determinant convention.

title: GRR calculation and the curve-theta sign
as_he_states: 59:6–9 asks for direct calculation and explicitly says to verify the sign;59:16 repeats the curve calculation for a complex of rankρ.
plausible_today: Compute the degree-two component of the Fourier–GRR transform, retaining the rank and whetherdet* meansdet or its inverse.
state_of_art: The exterior-algebra calculation gives½p_*(D²a_{n−1}). For the standard alternating determinant it is the negative theta class on a curve; the inverse determinant reverses this.
why_open: No convention-independent sign verdict is possible from an ambiguousdet* symbol. The missing rankρ is independently refuted by a rank-two example.
worth: High; fix the determinant convention before comparing the curve and abelian examples.

title: Universal-curve Picard sections and Franchetta
as_he_states: 59:10 asks that sections of the universal curve’s Picard functor be generated byK, including a marked point wheng=1.
plausible_today: Distinguish relative Picard sections from actual line bundles and include marked-point generators and low-genus exceptions.
state_of_art: Schröer’s strong Franchetta theorem covers the stated generic-curve setting forg≥3. The literal marked genus-one claim is false:K is trivial but the marked point has degree1.
why_open: The broad draft is not uniformly true. The relation between generic statements and sections on the entire moduli stack needs its own comparison.
worth: High; resolve the genus-one exception first and then state the genus≥3 theorem with its marking and field assumptions.

title: Which grading does the Chow Fourier transform reverse?
as_he_states: 59:10 says that expD transforms degreei into complementary degreen−i.
plausible_today: Distinguish cohomological degree from the Beauville bigrading of rational Chow groups.
state_of_art: Beauville1986 Prop1 givesCH^p_s→CH^{g−p+s}_s. Complementary codimension is the s=0 specialization.
why_open: The unrestricted Chow statement is false; the corrected graded statement is established.
worth: High; test a nonzeroPic⁰ class, whose Beauville grade is1, before applying complementary codimension.

title: Double determinant polarization and its sign
as_he_states: 59:10–11 says “faire calcul direct ... attention aux signes” and then writesφ(φ(δ))=δχ(δ)^{n−2}.
plausible_today: Separate the positive adjugate operationδ↦−φ(δ) fromφ itself.
state_of_art: With the standard determinant,φ=−adj andφ² has factor(−1)^g. The positive adjugate squared has the source’s positive factor.
why_open: The literal formula mixes two operations. Explicit diagonal calculations settle the algebra once a convention is fixed.
worth: High; useg=3 and a principal polarization as the first sign test.

title: Primitivity of the universal dual polarization
as_he_states: 59:11 expects the constructed polarization on the dual to be indivisible and generate the universal NS sections for the given degree.
plausible_today: Fix the full polarization type, not only its degree, and compare the adjugate polarization with the primitive dual type.
state_of_art: The type(1,2,2) has adjugate type(4,2,2), divisible by2. Thus the literal indivisibility expectation fails.
why_open: The primitive-generator version is a corrected moduli question; recent principal-level Franchetta results do not establish arbitrary-type statements.
worth: High; compute Smith invariants of the polarization map before making a universal generator claim.

title: Annihilator gcd versus canonical torsor trivialization
as_he_states: 59:12–14 compares powersλ and writesppcm after a crossed-outpgcd, while seeking canonical sections of polarization torsors.
plausible_today: Compute the common annihilator ideal generated byλ^g−λ^{g−1}, and separately ask whether the induced trivializations are compatible.
state_of_art: For g≥2 the gcd is2; forχλ^g−λ^{g−1} it is1 whenχ is even and2 whenχ is odd. Class annihilation does not select a canonical section.
why_open: The arithmetic is settled by an elementary proof. The asserted evenχ⇒2-divisible polarization is false, already in type(1,2).
worth: High; replace the arithmetic question by the ideal of annihilators while preserving the separate coherence question.

title: Compare two canonical doubled-polarization constructions
as_he_states: 59:28: “Vérifier que c’est la section ... canonique définie pour toute sectionδ ...”.
plausible_today: Compare the section of the doubled theta torsor from inversion with the normalized Poincaré pullback representing2λ.
state_of_art: Poonen–Stoll and Alexeev give the canonical2λ construction. For Jacobians, Serre duality identifies the doubled theta torsor section withK_C.
why_open: The all-base symbol-level comparison needs compatible rigidifications; merely proving2c_λ=0 does not prove equality of the two sections.
worth: High; compare the normalized fibre at the identity in both constructions.

title: Additivity in the coefficient complex
as_he_states: 59:15–17 generalizes the construction to a perfect complex and marks an additivity claim in the margin.
plausible_today: UseK₀-additivity inF and retain polynomial dependence on the tensor classδ of a line bundle.
state_of_art: Knudsen–Mumford gives determinant additivity; Fourier–GRR makesφ homogeneous of degreeg−1 inδ for abelian varieties.
why_open: The claim ofNS-additivity is false forg≥3. The correctedK₀ statement is established.
worth: High; testφ(2δ) on a principally polarized threefold before accepting the wordhomomorphism.

title: Tensor/translation equivariance signs
as_he_states: 59:18–20 twice requests verification of the signs in basepoint change and Pic⁰ translation.
plausible_today: With the positive kernel and h_M(β)=t_β*M⊗M^{-1}, the Picard-class difference is +h_M(β); the manuscript minus agrees if its tilde map is −h_M.
state_of_art: Mukai1981§3(3.1) supplies the exchange. The support of t_β*D moves by−β but gives no further minus in h_M; the explicit dictionary is in C-SA14-669.
why_open: The sign is convention dependent; the draft does not contain the requested completed check.
worth: High; compare the fibre of the transformed family atx with the old family atx+β.

title: Albanese duality from a chosen abelian subfunctor
as_he_states: 59:20–25 proposes starting the Albanese theory from B→Pic_X and asks how far the universal property extends to commutative groups.
plausible_today: Use a chosen abelian schemeB and its dual torsor recipient; treat arbitrary commutative group targets as a separate extension with extra hypotheses.
state_of_art: The abelian-target universal property is established in Milne and Laurent–Schröer. Proper connected varieties have no nonconstant maps to affine groups over a field, but that observation is not a blanket relative theorem.
why_open: The unrestricted target category in the margin is not fixed, so it is not declared solved by the abelian theorem.
worth: Medium; specify whether targets are smooth connected group schemes and whether the base is a field.

title: Canonical curve duality versus theta polarization
as_he_states: 59:24–25 asks whether the canonical duality is the theta polarization and tentatively inserts a sign;59:27 repeats “question de signe”.
plausible_today: Compare the diagonal-induced map with t_x^*L⊗L^{-1} after fixing the Albanese/Picard torsor action.

worth: High; calculate the degree-one Abel map for a pointed curve and compare the two induced homomorphisms.

title: Canonical theta torsor for a principally polarized abelian scheme
as_he_states: 59:26–28 constructs the unique A-equivariant pair(P,Θ) and its identification withPic^δ.
plausible_today: State the principal-polarization theta-pair equivalence over the base and distinguish it from arbitrary polarization-type torsor existence.
state_of_art: Alexeev2002§3.0.5–3.0.10 gives the explicit construction and equivalence. Laga2025 shows why broad arbitrary-type extrapolations require care.

worth: High historical match; compare the evaluation-at-zero divisor in the two constructions.

title: General separatedness of the correspondence functor
as_he_states: “I am convinced however that Corr is always separated” (57:23);57:32 asks the same question and proposes a fundamental-group specialization route.
plausible_today: For proper flatX,Y with universalH⁰=O, determine separatedness of normalized divisorial correspondences, including reducible fibres and algebraic-space Picard functors.
state_of_art: Murre1965 Th4 assumes separatedness and records the unrestricted assertion as a problem; separatedPic of either factor is a sufficient case. Modern algebraic-space representability suggests a route through the letter’s pre-ét case.
why_open: The cited Murre theorem does not by itself settle the general question. The full modern comparison is being treated as an exact-hypothesis question, not inferred from the theorem title.
worth: High; check whether Artin’s Picard-space theorem supplies every hypothesis of the letter’s pre-ét argument.

title: Local Picard theory without regular puncture

title: Locally free conormal module and smoothness in characteristic zero
as_he_states: 57:64 asks whether a group scheme over a base with characteristic-zero residue fields is smooth along its unit when its conormal module is locally free.
plausible_today: Add the explicit local finite-presentation hypothesis along the unit, then the stated condition is equivalent to smoothness there.
state_of_art: SGA3 VI B Proposition1.6 states exactly this equivalence; the proof uses the invariant-differential pullback and the EGA IV smoothness criterion.
why_open: Settled in the later published theorem. No flatness assumption needs to be invented to apply that proposition.
worth: High historical value, low new-research value; align this question with Proposition1.6 and keep it distinct from the full Picard-functor question.
